 Ashita Kashyap Updated: Nov 3, 2026, 11:05 IST ​School Holidays in November 2026 November 2026 brings festivals, regional holidays and weekly breaks that give school students an opportunity to enjoy the extended holidays. From Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kartik Purnima to Chhath Puja and state specific observances, the holiday calendar varies across India.
 Here is a state wise important November holiday dates, possible school holidays and what students and parents should know.
 November 2026 School Holidays: State wise vacation schedule 
 Students in different states are expected to get different holiday schedules. Some states have announced longer Diwali vacations, while others have listed holidays around individual festivals.
 The reported schedules are as follows:
 State Expected school holiday schedule 
 Maharashtra Diwali vacation: November 2-14 
 Goa Diwali vacation: November 2-21 
 Gujarat 21 day Diwali vacation: November 5-25 
 Bihar Diwali, Bhai Dooj and Chhath Puja: November 7-17 
 Uttar Pradesh Diwali-related holidays; additional regional holidays: November 8, 9 and 11 
 Jharkhand Festival holidays: November 9, 11, 16 and 17 
 Rajasthan Diwali vacation may run from November 4-15 
 The above table shows a state wise extended holiday in November 2026.
 The Goa Directorate of Education has officially notified its 2026-27 academic calendar, which confirms the Diwali vacation from November 2 to November 21 for the specified classes.
 Gujarat's 21 day vacation, from November 5 to November 25, has also been reported by All India Radio, citing the state Education Department's circular.
 In Bihar, the 2026 holiday calendar for government and government-aided schools lists a break from November 7 to November 17. 
 The schedule also includes November 24 as a holiday for Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kartik Purnima.
 Maharashtra schools are expected to observe a Diwali vacation from November 2 to November 14, while Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand have several individual festival holidays during the month.
 It is important to note, these dates should not be treated as a uniform holiday order for every school. Government, private, CBSE, ICSE and state board institutions may follow different calendars. 
 Parents should check their school's official circular before planning a trip.
 November 2026: Important festivals and their significance
 Diwali- November 8 
 Diwali, also known as Deepavali, is one of India's biggest festivals. Families celebrate the occasion by lighting diyas, decorating their homes, offering prayers and exchanging sweets. In 2026, Diwali falls on a Sunday, which means students in some states may not receive an additional holiday specifically for the festival.
 Govardhan Puja- November 9 
 Govardhan Puja is celebrated in honour of Lord Krishna. According to Hindu beliefs, Lord Krishna lifted Govardhan Hill to protect the people of Vrindavan from heavy rainfall. The festival is observed with prayers and offerings of food to the deity.
 Bhai Dooj- November 11 
 Bhai Dooj celebrates the special relationship between brothers and sisters. Sisters pray for their brothers' well-being and perform traditional rituals. 
 The festival is known as Bhau Beej in Maharashtra and Bhaiya Dooj in several northern states.
 Chhath Puja- November 15 
 Chhath Puja is one of the most important festivals in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Devotees worship the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya and observe strict fasting rituals. They offer prayers to the setting Sun and the rising Sun.
 Although the main Chhath Puja date falls on a Sunday in 2026, some states have additional holidays for the concluding rituals on November 16.
 Guru Nanak Jayanti- November 24 
 Guru Nanak Jayanti marks the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism and the first Sikh Guru. Devotees visit gurudwaras, participate in prayers and kirtans, and take part in community service.
 The festival coincides with Kartik Purnima in 2026 and falls on a Tuesday. It is a public holiday in several states.
 Will schools remain closed for the entire November festive season?
 Although November has important festivals, students will not get holidays for every one of them. 
 The actual number of days off depends on the state government's education calendar and the school's academic schedule.
 For students getting ready for board examinations, entrance tests and other competitive examinations, the extended Diwali break can also be a time to revise important chapters and finish any pending assignments.
 Parents should also keep in mind that some schools may shift their working days or change examination schedules to fit in vacations.
 With Diwali, Chhath Puja and Guru Nanak Jayanti all falling in November the month brings a mix of celebrations and longer breaks, for students. However the best way to know for sure is to check the school notice. That helps confirm reopening dates and prevents confusion.
